### Action Hierarchy Patterns

**Purpose:** Establish clear visual priority for user actions throughout the interface

#### Primary Actions
**When to Use:** Main action users should take (Submit, Approve, Confirm)

**Visual Design:**
- Gradient button (blue-purple per Gradient Energy design direction)
- High contrast with white text
- Prominent size (min 44x44px touch target)
- Box shadow on hover for depth

**Behavior:**
- Hover: Gradient brightens slightly, translateY(-1px), shadow increases
- Active: translateY(0), shadow reduces
- Loading: Spinner replaces text, button disabled
- Success: Checkmark animation, then fade to new state

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA label describes action clearly ("Submit timesheet to Factorial")
- Focus visible with 2px outline
- Keyboard: Enter or Space triggers action
- Screen reader announces loading and success states

**Mobile Considerations:**
- Full width on mobile (<640px)
- 48x48px minimum touch target
- Bottom-anchored for thumb reach

**Code Example:**
```typescript
<Button
  variant="gradient-primary"
  size="lg"
  onClick={handleSubmit}
  loading={isSubmitting}
  aria-label="Submit timesheet to Factorial"
>
  Submit
</Button>
```

#### Secondary Actions
**When to Use:** Alternative actions that support but don't advance the primary flow (Edit, Review Details, Request Changes)

**Visual Design:**
- Outline button with border
- Primary blue border and text
- No background fill (stays clean)
- Same size as primary for equal affordance

**Behavior:**
- Hover: Background fills with subtle primary blue (10% opacity)
- Active: Background deepens slightly
- Does not compete visually with primary action

**Accessibility:**
- Clear ARIA label
- Same keyboard support as primary
- Adequate contrast (4.5:1 minimum)

**Mobile Considerations:**
- Full width on mobile stacked below primary
- Same 48x48px minimum touch target

#### Tertiary Actions
**When to Use:** Low-priority actions or destructive actions (Cancel, Deny, Delete)

**Visual Design:**
- Ghost button (no border, no background)
- Muted text color for low priority
- Red text for destructive actions
- Smaller size acceptable (but maintain 44x44px target)

**Behavior:**
- Hover: Subtle background appears (muted gray for neutral, red/10% for destructive)
- Destructive actions require confirmation dialog

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA label includes warning for destructive actions
- Confirmation dialog for destructive actions with clear consequences
- "Are you sure?" pattern with Yes/No options

---

### Feedback Patterns

**Purpose:** Provide immediate, clear feedback for all user actions with consistent visual language

#### Success Feedback
**When to Use:** Action completed successfully (timesheet submitted, PTO approved)

**Visual Design:**
- **Toast notification:** Green background with white text, checkmark icon
- **Inline success state:** Green checkmark + "Success!" message
- **Celebration micro-interaction:** Subtle confetti or checkmark animation

**Behavior:**
- Toast appears top-right, auto-dismisses after 4 seconds
- User can dismiss early with X button
- Multiple toasts stack vertically

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA live region announces success (polite, not assertive)
- Icon + text + color (triple redundancy)
- Success message includes what happened ("Timesheet submitted to Factorial")

**Content Guidelines:**
- Be specific: "Timesheet submitted for Dec 18-22" not "Success!"
- Celebrate user accomplishment
- Include next steps if applicable

**Code Example:**
```typescript
toast.success("Timesheet submitted to Factorial! You're all set. ✅", {
  duration: 4000,
  ariaLive: "polite",
});
```

#### Error Feedback
**When to Use:** Action failed or validation error occurred

**Visual Design:**
- **Toast notification:** Red background, white text, error icon (⚠️)
- **Inline error:** Red text below field, red border on invalid field
- **Error summary:** Red card at top of form listing all errors

**Behavior:**
- Error toast persists until user dismisses (no auto-dismiss for errors)
- Focus moves to first error field on form submission failure
- Inline validation on blur (after first submission attempt)

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA live region announces error (assertive for critical errors)
- Error messages associated with fields via aria-describedby
- Clear instructions for fixing ("Hours must total 40 per week")

**Content Guidelines:**
- Explain what went wrong clearly
- Provide specific fix instructions
- Avoid technical jargon ("Connection failed" not "502 Bad Gateway")
- Offer help or escalation path when stuck

**Error Recovery:**
- Retry button for transient failures
- "Need help?" link to agent chat
- Save draft for later completion

#### Warning Feedback
**When to Use:** User should review before proceeding (approval with risks, policy exceptions)

**Visual Design:**
- **Inline warning:** Amber background, warning icon (⚠️), dark text
- **Warning badge:** Amber badge on approval cards
- **Modal confirmation:** For high-stakes warnings

**Behavior:**
- Doesn't block action but encourages review
- Can be dismissed after reading
- Escalates to modal for critical warnings

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA role="alert" for important warnings
- Icon + text + color redundancy
- Clear indication of what's at risk

**Content Guidelines:**
- State the risk clearly ("Team coverage only 50%")
- Explain consequences ("Project delivery may be impacted")
- Offer mitigation ("Review with team before approving")

#### Info Feedback
**When to Use:** Helpful context or status updates (learning in progress, background sync)

**Visual Design:**
- **Info badge:** Blue background, info icon (ℹ️)
- **Subtle inline message:** Blue-gray background, non-intrusive

**Behavior:**
- Auto-dismisses after 6 seconds
- Doesn't interrupt user flow
- Can be dismissed immediately

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA live region (polite, non-intrusive)
- Optional reading (users can skip without missing critical info)

---

### Conversational Patterns

**Purpose:** Establish consistent conversational interaction patterns for AI chat interface

#### Message Streaming Pattern
**When to Use:** Agent responding to user message with generated content

**Visual Design:**
- Message bubble appears with "Agent is thinking..." indicator
- Text streams in character-by-character at readable pace (30-50 chars/sec)
- Cursor animation at end of streaming text
- Message complete indicator (timestamp appears)

**Behavior:**
- Auto-scroll viewport to keep new content visible
- User can scroll up without interrupting stream
- Streaming pauses if user scrolls up, resumes when at bottom

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA live region announces message as it completes (not character-by-character)
- Screen reader users get complete message, not fragmented
- "Agent is responding" announced when streaming begins

**Performance:**
- Buffer chunks to avoid jank
- Graceful degradation to instant display on slow connections

#### Progressive Disclosure Pattern
**When to Use:** Agent response contains detailed information that might overwhelm user

**Visual Design:**
- Summary displayed by default (1-2 sentences)
- "Show details" link or button
- Expandable section with smooth animation
- "Hide details" option after expanding

**Behavior:**
- Expand animation: 300ms ease-in-out
- Auto-scroll to reveal expanded content
- Remember user's expand/collapse preferences per message type

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA expanded state toggles
- Focus moves into expanded content
- Keyboard: Enter to expand, Escape to collapse

**Content Guidelines:**
- Summary should be self-sufficient for quick decisions
- Details provide validation and transparency
- Don't hide critical decision factors in collapsed state

#### Quick Reply Pattern
**When to Use:** Agent offers predefined response options (Yes/No, Accept/Edit/Reject)

**Visual Design:**
- Horizontal button row below agent message
- Outline buttons with icons
- Max 3-4 options (more use dropdown)

**Behavior:**
- Clicking sends that response immediately
- Buttons disable after selection
- Agent responds to selected option

**Accessibility:**
- Buttons in tab order
- ARIA labels describe action outcome
- Keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter)

**Mobile Considerations:**
- Stack vertically on narrow screens (<640px)
- Full-width buttons for easy tapping

#### Contextual Help Pattern
**When to Use:** User appears stuck or confused

**Visual Design:**
- Subtle "Need help?" link in message
- Help tooltip with suggestions
- Option to escalate to detailed assistance

**Behavior:**
- Appears after user hesitation (30+ seconds no input)
- Dismissible without penalty
- Offers relevant suggestions based on context

**Accessibility:**
- Not intrusive (polite ARIA announcement)
- Keyboard accessible
- Clear escape path (dismiss easily)

---

### Decision Support Patterns

**Purpose:** Consistent patterns for displaying risk, confidence, and decision context

#### Risk Indicator Pattern
**When to Use:** Displaying AI assessment of decision risk (approval cards, exception packages)

**Visual Design:**
- Color-coded badge with icon + text
- **Green (✅):** "Safe to Approve" - no significant risks
- **Yellow (⚠️):** "Review Needed" - medium risk, specific concerns
- **Red (🚫):** "Risk Detected" - high risk, recommend alternative

**Behavior:**
- Appears prominently at top of decision card
- Hover shows tooltip with reasoning summary
- Click expands full risk explanation

**Accessibility:**
- Icon + text + color (triple redundancy)
- ARIA label describes full risk level
- Tooltip keyboard-accessible

**Content Guidelines:**
- Lead with risk level
- State specific concern (not generic warning)
- Offer mitigation when possible

#### Confidence Indicator Pattern
**When to Use:** Displaying AI confidence in suggestions (timesheet suggestions, predictions)

**Visual Design:**
- Percentage badge (95% confident)
- Color-coded: High (green), Medium (amber), Low (red)
- Source citation ("Based on your calendar")

**Behavior:**
- Always visible with suggestion
- Tooltip explains confidence factors
- Transparent about uncertainty

**Accessibility:**
- Percentage read by screen reader
- Color supports but doesn't convey sole meaning
- Confidence level in ARIA label

**Content Guidelines:**
- Be transparent about confidence level
- Cite sources explicitly
- Lower confidence = more review encouraged

#### Precedent Display Pattern
**When to Use:** Showing historical decisions that inform current decision (exception handling)

**Visual Design:**
- Compact card listing similar past cases
- Date, outcome, and brief description
- "3 similar cases, all approved" summary

**Behavior:**
- Collapsed by default (count visible)
- Expands to show individual cases
- Click case to see full details

**Accessibility:**
- Summary announces count and outcomes
- Individual cases keyboard-navigable
- Clear association with current decision

---

### Form & Input Patterns

**Purpose:** Consistent data collection and validation patterns

#### Inline Validation Pattern
**When to Use:** Real-time validation of user input

**Visual Design:**
- Green checkmark appears when valid
- Red error message appears on blur if invalid
- Yellow warning for concerns (not blocking)

**Behavior:**
- Validate on blur (not every keystroke)
- After first submit attempt, validate on change
- Don't clear valid state on focus (keep checkmark)

**Accessibility:**
- Error message associated via aria-describedby
- Error announced politely (not every keystroke)
- Success state also announced

**Content Guidelines:**
- Specific error message ("Must be 0-24 hours")
- Positive tone when possible ("Almost there!")
- Avoid negative language

#### Inline Editing Pattern
**When to Use:** Editing data in place without modal (timesheet hours, project allocation)

**Visual Design:**
- Click to edit (field becomes editable)
- Show edit affordance on hover (pencil icon)
- Save/Cancel buttons appear inline

**Behavior:**
- Single-click to edit (not double-click)
- Tab to next editable field
- Enter saves, Escape cancels
- Optimistic update (instant visual feedback)

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA label indicates editable
- Edit mode announced clearly
- Keyboard: Enter to save, Escape to cancel

#### Autocomplete Pattern
**When to Use:** Helping users select from known options (project names, employee names)

**Visual Design:**
- Dropdown appears below field
- Matched text highlighted
- Max 8 suggestions (scroll for more)

**Behavior:**
- Search as user types (debounced 300ms)
- Keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Enter to select)
- Click outside or Escape to dismiss

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA combobox role
- Selected option announced
- Count of options available

---

### Loading & Empty States

**Purpose:** Provide clarity during loading and handle empty data gracefully

#### Skeleton Loading Pattern
**When to Use:** Fetching data for cards, tables, lists

**Visual Design:**
- Gray placeholder matching content structure
- Subtle shimmer animation (pulse)
- Same layout as real content

**Behavior:**
- Appears immediately (no spinner delay)
- Morphs into real content when loaded
- Progressive loading (show what you have)

**Accessibility:**
- ARIA live region announces "Loading..."
- Announces completion with content summary

#### Streaming Content Pattern
**When to Use:** SSE streaming from AI agent

**Visual Design:**
- Content appears progressively
- Cursor animation at end during streaming
- Smooth fade-in for new content

**Behavior:**
- Auto-scroll to keep new content visible
- User can interrupt (stop reading)
- Completion indicator appears

#### Empty State Pattern
**When to Use:** No data exists yet (empty exception queue, no PTO requests)

**Visual Design:**
- Illustration or icon centered
- Helpful message explaining why it's empty
- Call-to-action button if applicable

**Behavior:**
- Encourages action if appropriate
- Explains what will appear here
- Not an error (neutral tone)

**Content Guidelines:**
- Positive framing ("No exceptions! Team is running smoothly")
- Explain what this space is for
- Guide user to first action if needed

---

### Error Recovery Patterns

**Purpose:** Help users recover from errors gracefully

#### Retry Pattern
**When to Use:** Transient failure (network error, temporary API failure)

**Visual Design:**
- Error message with "Retry" button
- Loading spinner on retry
- Success toast when recovered

**Behavior:**
- Retry with exponential backoff
- Max 3 auto-retries, then ask user
- Preserve user input during retries

**Accessibility:**
- Announces retry attempt
- Announces success or final failure
- Clear next steps if all retries fail

#### Offline Mode Pattern
**When to Use:** Network connection lost

**Visual Design:**
- Banner at top: "You're offline. Changes will sync when reconnected."
- Queued actions shown in list
- Auto-hide banner when reconnected

**Behavior:**
- Continue allowing read operations
- Queue write operations
- Auto-sync when connection restored
- Notify user of sync success

**Accessibility:**
- Offline status announced
- Reconnection announced
- Queued actions count announced

#### Escalation Pattern
**When to Use:** User is stuck, errors persist, or needs human help

**Visual Design:**
- "Need help?" link in error message
- Opens agent chat with pre-filled context
- Option to contact support directly

**Behavior:**
- Pre-fill chat with error context
- Agent has full error details
- Seamless handoff to human if needed

**Accessibility:**
- Help option clearly announced
- Keyboard accessible
- Context preserved through escalation

---

### Modal & Dialog Patterns

**Purpose:** Focused interactions requiring user attention

#### Confirmation Dialog Pattern
**When to Use:** Destructive actions (deny PTO, delete exception)

**Visual Design:**
- Modal overlay dims background
- Dialog centered, max 500px width
- Clear title stating action
- Explanation of consequences
- Primary action (destructive) and Cancel

**Behavior:**
- Appears with fade animation
- Focus traps in dialog
- Escape closes (same as Cancel)
- Click overlay closes (same as Cancel)

**Accessibility:**
- Focus moves to dialog on open
- Tab cycles within dialog only
- Escape and overlay click close dialog
- Focus returns to trigger on close
- ARIA role="alertdialog" for destructive

**Content Guidelines:**
- Title is action ("Deny PTO Request?")
- Explain consequences clearly
- Destructive action button is red
- "Are you sure?" pattern

#### Information Dialog Pattern
**When to Use:** Showing expanded details (full audit trail, calendar view)

**Visual Design:**
- Larger modal (up to 90% viewport)
- Close button top-right
- Scrollable content area
- Footer with actions if needed

**Behavior:**
- Smooth slide-up animation
- Body scroll locked
- Escape or X closes
- Actions in footer (if applicable)

**Accessibility:**
- Focus management same as confirmation
- Scrollable region properly marked
- Close button labeled clearly

---

### Navigation Patterns

**Purpose:** Consistent navigation within HRAgent

#### Chat-Centric Navigation Pattern
**When to Use:** Primary navigation pattern for HRAgent

**Visual Design:**
- Chat interface is always present (not hidden)
- Side panel for dashboard/admin (collapsible)
- Breadcrumbs for context
- Back button returns to chat

**Behavior:**
- Chat persists across views
- Dashboard overlays or side-by-side
- Deep links open in context

**Accessibility:**
- Skip links to main content
- Keyboard navigation (Tab order logical)
- Current location announced

#### Context Preservation Pattern
**When to Use:** User navigates away and returns

**Visual Design:**
- Conversation history preserved
- Scroll position restored
- Draft messages saved

**Behavior:**
- Chat state saved in session
- Automatic draft save (debounced)
- "Resume conversation" on return

**Accessibility:**
- Announces preserved context
- Scroll position restored

---

**What would you like to do?**

[A] Advanced Elicitation - Refine UX patterns with deeper discovery  
[P] Party Mode - Bring design and dev perspectives  
[C] Continue - Save to document and move to responsive & accessibility

Please check your network and try again.", action: { label: "Retry", onClick: handleRetry, }, duration: Infinity, // Persists until dismissed }); ``` #### Warning Feedback **When to Use:** User should review before proceeding (approval with risks, policy exceptions, potential conflicts) **Visual Design:** - **Inline warning card:** Amber background (`var(--warning)` with 10% opacity), dark text, warning icon (⚠️) - **Warning badge:** Amber badge with "Review Needed" or "Caution" label - **Modal confirmation:** For high-stakes warnings that require explicit acknowledgment - **Left border accent:** 4px amber border on warning cards **Behavior:** - Doesn't block action but encourages thoughtful review - Can be dismissed after reading ("I understand" button) - Escalates to modal for critical warnings (>70% risk level) - Remembers dismissal per session (doesn't re-show immediately) **Accessibility:** - ARIA `role="alert"` for important warnings - Icon + text + color redundancy (amber may be hard to distinguish) - Clear indication of what's at risk: "Team coverage only 50% during this period" - Explanation of consequences: "Project delivery may be impacted" **Content Guidelines:** - State the specific concern clearly: "Team coverage only 50%" - Explain potential consequences: "This may impact the Q1 launch on March 15" - Offer mitigation options: "Review with team before approving" or "Suggest alternative dates" - Use "Review needed" language rather than "Warning" (less alarming) **Implementation Example:** ```typescript Review Needed Team coverage only 50% during this period. The Q1 launch on March 15 may be impacted. Consider discussing with the team before approving. ``` #### Info Feedback **When to Use:** Helpful context, status updates, or educational content (learning in progress, background sync, tips) **Visual Design:** - **Info badge:** Blue background (`var(--info)` or muted blue), info icon (ℹ️) - **Subtle inline message:** Blue-gray background, non-intrusive, can include icon - **Tooltip on hover:** Small popover with additional context **Behavior:** - Auto-dismisses after 6 seconds (longer than success for reading time) - Doesn't interrupt user flow (appears in non-blocking location) - Can be dismissed immediately if user wishes - Doesn't steal focus or interrupt current action **Accessibility:** - ARIA live region with `aria-live="polite"` (non-intrusive) - Optional reading (users can skip without missing critical information) - Tooltip accessible via keyboard focus (Tab to element, tooltip appears) **Content Guidelines:** - Provide helpful context without being annoying - Educational tone: "Tip: You can say 'log my hours' to submit timesheets" - Status updates: "Learning your patterns... suggestions will improve over time" - Keep brief (1-2 sentences maximum) **Implementation Example:** ```typescript toast.info("Learning your patterns", { description: "HRAgent is analyzing your work habits to provide better suggestions.", duration: 6000, icon: , }); ``` --- ### Conversational Patterns **Purpose:** Establish consistent conversational interaction patterns for the AI chat interface that feel natural and responsive. #### Message Streaming Pattern **When to Use:** Agent responding to user message with AI-generated content via SSE **Visual Design:** - Message bubble appears with "HRAgent is thinking..." indicator (animated dots) - Text streams in character-by-character at readable pace (30-50 characters/second) - Blinking cursor animation at end of streaming text - Message completion indicated by timestamp appearance and cursor removal **Behavior:** - Auto-scroll viewport to keep newest content visible (smooth scroll behavior) - User can scroll up to review previous messages without interrupting stream - **Streaming pauses** if user scrolls up (>100px from bottom), resumes when user scrolls to bottom - Buffer SSE chunks to avoid text jank (render in batches of 5-10 chars) - Graceful degradation: falls back to instant display if SSE fails **Accessibility:** - ARIA live region announces message **when complete**, not character-by-character - "HRAgent is responding" announced when streaming begins - Screen reader users receive complete coherent message - Visual users see progressive streaming for perceived speed **Performance Optimization:** - Buffer chunks to avoid layout thrashing - RequestAnimationFrame for smooth text appearance - Debounce scroll events (check position every 100ms max) - Virtualize message history (only render visible + 10 messages) **Implementation Example:** ```typescript const streamMessage = async (content: string) => { const chars = content.split(''); let displayedContent = ''; for (const char of chars) { displayedContent += char; setMessageContent(displayedContent); await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20)); // 50 chars/sec } setStreamingComplete(true); }; ``` #### Progressive Disclosure Pattern **When to Use:** Agent response contains detailed information that might overwhelm users if shown all at once **Visual Design:** - **Summary displayed by default** (1-2 sentences, most important info) - **"Show details" link/button** with down chevron icon - Expandable section with smooth height animation (300ms ease-in-out) - **"Hide details" option** after expanding (up chevron, same position) **Behavior:** - Expand animation: smooth height transition, content fades in - Auto-scroll to reveal expanded content if it extends below viewport - Remember user's expand/collapse preferences per message type (localStorage) - Can have nested levels (summary → details → deep details) **Accessibility:** - `aria-expanded` state toggles between true/false - Focus moves into expanded content after animation completes - Keyboard: Enter or Space to expand, Escape to collapse - Screen reader announces "Expanded" or "Collapsed" state change **Content Guidelines:** - Summary should be self-sufficient for quick decisions - Details provide validation, transparency, and deeper context - Don't hide critical decision factors in collapsed state - Use progressive layers: summary (always visible) → details (1 click) → deep details (2 clicks) **Implementation Example:** ```typescript

Safe to approve." - Tooltip accessible via keyboard (focus + hover) - High contrast mode: borders distinguish risk levels without color **Content Guidelines:** - Lead with risk level in clear language ("Safe" / "Caution" / "Risk") - State specific concern, not generic warning: "Team coverage only 50%" not "There may be issues" - Offer mitigation when possible: "Consider discussing with team before approving" - Transparent about confidence: "95% confident based on team calendars" **Implementation Example:** ```typescript {risk === 'green' && } {risk === 'yellow' && } {risk === 'red' && } {riskLabel} ``` #### Confidence Indicator Pattern **When to Use:** Displaying AI confidence in suggestions, predictions, or pattern recognition (timesheet suggestions, PTO forecasts) **Visual Design:** - **Percentage badge:** "95% confident" with color coding - **Color scale:** High (>90% green), Medium (70-90% amber), Low (<70% red) - **Source citation:** "Based on your calendar" or "Like last 4 weeks" - Small inline badge or larger card header depending on prominence needed **Behavior:** - Always visible with AI-generated suggestions (transparency principle) - Tooltip explains confidence factors: "Based on 8 weeks of pattern data" - Lower confidence triggers additional explanations or user confirmation - Confidence displayed as both percentage and semantic label **Accessibility:** - Percentage announced by screen reader: "95 percent confident" - Color supports meaning but doesn't convey it alone - Confidence level included in ARIA label: "High confidence suggestion" - Tooltip provides full explanation for validation **Content Guidelines:** - Be transparent about confidence level (builds trust) - Cite sources explicitly: "Based on your calendar meetings" or "Similar to last 4 weeks" - Lower confidence = encourage more review: "Please verify this suggestion" - Explain what influenced confidence: "High confidence due to consistent pattern" **Implementation Example:** ```typescript

All changes synced." **Implementation Example:** ```typescript {isOffline && ( You're offline Changes are saved locally and will sync when you reconnect. {queuedItems > 0 && ` (${queuedItems} items queued)`} )} ``` #### Escalation Pattern **When to Use:** User is stuck, errors persist, or complex situation needs human judgment **Visual Design:** - **"Need help?" link** in error messages or after repeated failures - **Opens agent chat** with pre-filled error context - **Option to contact support** directly for critical issues **Behavior:** - Pre-fill chat with complete error context (user doesn't need to re-explain) - Agent has full error details, stack trace, user actions leading to error - Seamless handoff to human support if agent can't resolve - Context preserved throughout escalation chain **Accessibility:** - Help option clearly announced in error message - Keyboard accessible (Tab to "Need help?" link, Enter to open) - Context preservation announced - Smooth transition to chat interface **Content Guidelines:** - Empathetic tone: "I can help you with that" - No shame: "This is tricky, let's figure it out together" - Clear escalation: "I'll connect you with someone who can help" - Preserve dignity: "You didn't do anything wrong" **Implementation Example:** ```typescript toast.error("Unable to submit timesheet", { description: "I've tried several times but the submission keeps failing.", action: { label: "Get Help", onClick: () => openChatWithContext({ issue: "timesheet_submission_failure", errorDetails: error, userActions: actions, }), }, }); They'll be notified immediately." - **Destructive button is red:** "Deny Request" - **Cancel is neutral:** "Cancel" or "Go Back" **Implementation Example:** ```typescript Deny PTO Request? Jamie's request for March 10-12 will be denied. They'll be notified immediately and won't be able to take these days off. Cancel Deny Request ``` #### Information Dialog Pattern **When to Use:** Showing expanded details (full audit trail, detailed calendar view, help documentation) **Visual Design:** - **Larger modal** (up to 90% viewport width/height) - Scrollable region properly marked with ARIA - Close button clearly labeled: "Close dialog" - Keyboard: Tab through content, Escape to close **Implementation Example:** ```typescript Complete Audit Trail Full history of this exception from submission to resolution ``` --- ### Navigation Patterns **Purpose:** Consistent navigation within HRAgent that maintains context and supports both casual and power users. #### Chat-Centric Navigation Pattern **When to Use:** Primary navigation pattern throughout HRAgent application **Visual Design:** - **Chat interface always present** (main column, never hidden) - **Side panel for dashboard/admin** (collapsible on mobile) - **Breadcrumbs** show current context at top - **Back button** returns to previous chat state **Behavior:** - Chat persists across all views (conversation state maintained) - Dashboard/admin opens in side panel or overlay (doesn't replace chat) - Deep links open in context (chat + relevant panel) - Navigation doesn't interrupt ongoing conversations **Accessibility:** - **Skip links** to main content areas ("Skip to chat", "Skip to dashboard") - Keyboard navigation with logical Tab order - Current location announced by screen reader - Landmark regions properly marked (main, navigation, complementary) **Mobile Considerations:** - Chat fullscreen by default on mobile - Dashboard accessible via hamburger menu or bottom nav - Swipe gestures for panel transitions **Implementation Example:** ```typescript

## Responsive Design & Accessibility

Based on the PRD platform requirements (web SPA, mobile-first, 320px-1024px+ range) and our Gradient Energy design direction, I'll define comprehensive responsive and accessibility strategies for HRAgent.

### Responsive Strategy

**Mobile-First Approach:** HRAgent prioritizes mobile experience since employees like Sarah submit timesheets on-the-go and managers like Marcus approve requests between meetings.

#### Mobile Strategy (320px - 767px)

**Layout:**
- Single-column vertical stacking (all content full-width)
- Bottom-anchored primary actions for natural thumb reach
- Collapsible sections default to collapsed (preserve vertical space)
- Chat interface takes full screen (dashboard accessed via menu)

**Interaction Optimizations:**
- 48x48px minimum touch targets (exceeds 44px standard)
- Swipe gestures for common actions (swipe left to delete draft, swipe right for options)
- Pull-to-refresh for message history and approval queues
- Bottom sheet modals (easier one-handed operation than center modals)

**Content Density:**
- Show essential information only (approval risk level, employee name, dates)
- Progressive disclosure for details (tap "Show details" to expand)
- Inline actions reduced to 1-2 primary choices
- Navigation via bottom tab bar (Chat / Dashboard / Profile)

**Performance:**
- Aggressive image optimization (WebP format, lazy loading)
- Code splitting by route (chat core loads first)
- Skeleton UI for instant perceived load
- Service worker for offline capability

**Mobile-Specific Features:**
- Voice input for timesheet submission ("Log my hours")
- Camera access for document attachment (policy questions)
- Push notifications for reminders (browser notifications)
- Add to homescreen prompt (PWA installation)

#### Tablet Strategy (768px - 1023px)

**Layout:**
- Two-column layout (chat + sidebar panel for context)
- Side navigation visible (no hamburger menu)
- Approval cards show more detail by default
- Modal dialogs larger (utilize screen real estate)

**Interaction Model:**
- Mix of touch and mouse interaction support
- Hover states active (tablets may use mouse/trackpad)
- Keyboard shortcuts available (iPad keyboard users)
- Drag-and-drop for reordering (exception queue priority)

**Content Density:**
- Medium density (between mobile and desktop)
- Approval cards show summary + key details
- Chat messages show inline actions without expansion
- Dashboard widgets visible in sidebar

#### Desktop Strategy (1024px+)

**Layout:**
- Three-column layout (navigation + chat + context panel)
- Persistent side navigation (no collapse needed)
- Dashboard overlays chat in split view
- Exception queue visible alongside chat for Priya

**Desktop-Specific Features:**
- **Command palette** (Cmd/Ctrl+K for power users like Marcus)
- Keyboard shortcuts for all common actions
- Multi-select for batch operations (approve multiple PTO requests)
- Richer data visualizations (team calendar, coverage heatmaps)
- Hover tooltips with detailed context

**Information Density:**
- High density for admin views (Priya's exception queue)
- More cards visible per view (less scrolling)
- Approval cards show expanded details by default
- Full audit trails inline (no separate modal needed)

**Window Management:**
- Resizable panels (adjust chat vs. dashboard ratio)
- Remember panel sizes per user
- Keyboard focus management across panels

---

### Breakpoint Strategy

**Mobile-First Media Queries:** Start with mobile layout, progressively enhance for larger screens.

**Breakpoint Definitions:**

**Content Max-Width:**
- Chat messages: max 640px (optimal reading length)
- Approval cards: max 800px (maintain card proportion)
- Dashboard: max 1400px (prevent excessive width)
- Full-width elements: exception queue tables, analytics dashboards

**Layout Transitions:**

**Component Behavior by Breakpoint:**

| Component | Mobile (<768px) | Tablet (768-1023px) | Desktop (1024px+) |
|-----------|----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **Navigation** | Bottom tabs | Side rail | Persistent sidebar |
| **Chat** | Full screen | Main column (60%) | Center column (50%) |
| **Approval Cards** | Full width | Max 600px | Max 800px |
| **Actions** | Stacked vertical | Horizontal row | Horizontal with shortcuts |
| **Modals** | Bottom sheet | Center (80% width) | Center (max 800px) |
| **Dashboard** | Full screen view | Sidebar (40%) | Right panel (30%) |
| **Exception Queue** | List view | Table view (compact) | Table view (detailed) |

**Responsive Images:**
**Responsive Typography:**

---

### Accessibility Strategy

**WCAG Compliance Level: AA (Industry Standard)**

HRAgent targets WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, which is the industry standard and provides good accessibility without excessive implementation cost. This level is appropriate because:
- HRAgent is used in enterprise/workplace context (legal compliance requirements)
- Users may have diverse abilities (color blindness, motor impairments, screen reader users)
- AA provides excellent usability improvements that benefit all users

## Responsive Design & Accessibility HRAgent is designed mobile-first to support employees submitting timesheets on-the-go and managers approving requests between meetings. This section defines how the interface adapts across devices and ensures accessibility for all users. ### Responsive Strategy **Mobile-First Approach:** Prioritizing mobile experience since Sarah submits timesheets from her phone and Marcus approves PTO requests on his iPad. #### Mobile Strategy (320px - 767px) **Layout:** - Single-column vertical stacking (all content full-width) - Bottom-anchored primary actions for natural thumb reach - Collapsible sections default to collapsed (preserve vertical space) - Chat interface takes full screen (dashboard accessed via hamburger menu) **Interaction Optimizations:** - **48x48px minimum touch targets** (exceeds 44px WCAG standard for better usability) - Swipe gestures for common actions (swipe approval cards for quick actions) - Pull-to-refresh for message history and approval queues - Bottom sheet modals (easier one-handed operation than centered modals) **Content Density:** - Show essential information only (risk level, employee name, dates) - Progressive disclosure for details (tap "Show details" to expand) - Inline actions reduced to 1-2 primary choices - Navigation via bottom tab bar (Chat / Approvals / Profile) **Performance Optimizations:** - Aggressive image optimization (WebP format, lazy loading) - Code splitting by route (chat core loads first, <2s TTI) - Skeleton UI for instant perceived load - Service worker for offline capability (queue actions when offline) **Mobile-Specific Features:** - Voice input capability for timesheet submission ("Log my hours") - Camera access for document attachment (policy questions) - Push notifications for reminders (browser notifications API) - Add to homescreen prompt (PWA installation for app-like experience) #### Tablet Strategy (768px - 1023px) **Layout:** - Two-column layout (chat main column + sidebar panel for context) - Side navigation visible (no hamburger menu collapse) - Approval cards show more detail by default - Modal dialogs larger to utilize screen real estate **Interaction Model:** - Hybrid touch and mouse interaction support - Hover states active (tablets may use mouse/trackpad accessories) - Keyboard shortcuts available (iPad Magic Keyboard users) - Drag-and-drop for reordering (exception queue priority management) **Content Density:** - Medium density (between mobile and desktop) - Approval cards show summary + key context details - Chat messages show inline action buttons without expansion - Dashboard widgets visible in sidebar panel #### Desktop Strategy (1024px+) **Layout:** - Three-column layout (navigation + chat + context panel) - Persistent side navigation (no collapse needed) - Dashboard overlays chat in split view for admin - Exception queue visible alongside chat for Priya's workflow **Desktop-Specific Features:** - **Command palette** (Cmd/Ctrl+K) for power users like Marcus - Comprehensive keyboard shortcuts for all common actions - Multi-select for batch operations (approve multiple PTO requests) - Richer data visualizations (team calendar heatmaps, coverage charts) - Detailed hover tooltips with expanded context **Information Density:** - High density for admin views (Priya's exception queue) - More cards visible per viewport (reduced scrolling) - Approval cards show expanded details by default - Full audit trails inline (no separate modal needed) **Window Management:** - Resizable panels (adjust chat vs. dashboard ratio) - User preferences saved per session (panel sizes, collapsed states) - Keyboard focus management across multiple panels --- ### Breakpoint Strategy **Mobile-First Media Queries:** Start with mobile layout as base, progressively enhance for larger screens. **Breakpoint Definitions:** ```css /* Mobile: Base styles (320px+) */ /* No media query needed - this is the default */ /* Phablet: Enhanced mobile (480px+) */ @media (min-width: 480px) { /* Slightly wider cards, two-column action button layouts */ } /* Tablet Portrait: Two-column layouts begin (768px+) */ @media (min-width: 768px) { /* Sidebar appears, chat + context panel split view */ } /* Tablet Landscape / Small Desktop (1024px+) */ @media (min-width: 1024px) { /* Three-column layout, persistent navigation sidebar */ } /* Desktop (1280px+) */ @media (min-width: 1280px) { /* Wider content max-width, richer data visualizations */ } /* Large Desktop (1536px+) */ @media (min-width: 1536px) { /* Additional context panels, dashboard + chat truly side-by-side */ } ``` **Tailwind CSS Configuration:** ```typescript // tailwind.config.js module.exports = { theme: { screens: { 'sm': '480px', // Enhanced mobile 'md': '768px', // Tablet portrait 'lg': '1024px', // Tablet landscape / small desktop 'xl': '1280px', // Desktop '2xl': '1536px', // Large desktop }, }, }; ``` **Content Max-Width Constraints:** - Chat messages: max 640px (optimal reading length, 50-75 characters) - Approval cards: max 800px (maintain card proportions) - Dashboard panels: max 1400px (prevent excessive width on large monitors) - Full-width elements: exception queue tables, analytics dashboards (utilize space) **Component Behavior by Breakpoint:** | Component | Mobile (<768px) | Tablet (768-1023px) | Desktop (1024px+) | |-----------|----------------|---------------------|-------------------| | **Navigation** | Bottom tabs (3-4 items) | Side rail (icons + labels) | Persistent sidebar (full labels) | | **Chat** | Full screen | Main column (60% width) | Center column (50% width) | | **Approval Cards** | Full width | Max 600px centered | Max 800px centered | | **Action Buttons** | Stacked vertical | Horizontal row | Horizontal with keyboard shortcuts | | **Modals** | Bottom sheet slide-up | Center modal (80% width) | Center modal (max 800px) | | **Dashboard** | Full screen overlay | Sidebar (40% width) | Right panel (30% width) | | **Exception Queue** | Card list view | Compact table view | Detailed table view | | **Timesheet Entry** | Single day at a time | Week view (scrollable) | Full week grid | **Responsive Typography:** ```css :root { /* Consistent 16px base across all devices for readability */ --font-size-body: 16px; --line-height-body: 1.5; } @media (min-width: 768px) { :root { --line-height-body: 1.6; /* More breathing room on larger screens */ } } ``` **Responsive Images:** ```tsx ``` --- ### Accessibility Strategy **WCAG Compliance Level: 2.1 Level AA (Industry Standard)** HRAgent targets WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, appropriate for enterprise workplace applications with diverse user abilities. **Rationale for AA Level:** -
